correctness.rationale: Using the displayed Q_i with omega^2+omega+1=0, the exact factor Q2-Q3=3(omega-omega^2)(X-Y)(7(X+Y)+2Z) reduces their intersection to two quadratic and two rational projective points. A fresh SymPy polynomial remainder verified that factorization and Q1([-7:5:7])=2457. Each conic determinant -256 excludes reducibility in odd characteristic; the third-conic evaluations 2457=3^3*7*13 and product -3^5*13 prevent triple intersections outside 7,13. Distinctness and transversality give exactly 12 ordinary nodes. The two independent quadratic involutions have fixed-node counts 12,6,4,2, yielding Frobenius formula and Chebotarev density. p=7 creates triple incidence; p=13 collides quadratic points. Excludes p=2,3; finite Jacobian checks corroborate, not prove all-prime theorem.

value.rationale: The arithmetic splitting-field/Frobenius classification for a canonical curve arrangement is a motivated exact invariant: it determines when all singularities are rational and isolates the two genuine bad primes. It is not merely a re-count of the known twelve complex nodes.

final_claim: For the three fixed hyperosculating conics of X^3+Y^3-XYZ=0, the twelve ordinary nodes of their union split over K=Q(sqrt(-3),sqrt(13)), with biquadratic orbits (1,1,2,2,2,4). For every prime p>=5 outside {7,13}, reduction retains twelve geometric nodes; rational fixed-node counts by Legendre pair ((-3/p),(13/p)) are 12,6,4,2, each on density 1/4 of primes. Exactly 7 and 13 are exceptional reductions among primes >=5.
limitations: Original arrangement and geometric twelve nodes credited to Dimca et al.; no claim of novelty for geometric incidence.
Full exceptional singularity baskets at p=7,13 and behavior at p=2,3 are outside scope.
